subtitle: From Civil War to Kanchi-Kaveri: The Humbling of a Gajapati

panels.shot: low-angle wide of a royal figure in armor holding a broom beside a towering temple chariot, distant fort silhouettes on the horizon
panels.action: Purushottama Deva stands between a colossal wooden chariot of Jagannath and the shadowy outlines of southern hill forts, one hand on a ceremonial broom, the other resting on his sword, as monsoon clouds gather over Puri.

dialogue.text: He was mocked as the king who swept a god’s chariot, yet his answer to that insult was a war that carried Odisha’s banners to Kanchi and the Kaveri.

i18n.hi: जिस राजा को देवता की रथ-झाड़ू के लिए हँसाया गया, उसने उसी ताने का जवाब ऐसी जंग से दिया कि ओड़िशा का ध्वज कांची से कावेरी तक लहराया।

panels.shot: somber interior medium shot, throne room lit by oil lamps, focus on a young king’s tense profile
panels.action: In the dim audience hall at Cuttack, the young Purushottama Deva sits rigid on the Gajapati throne, elders and captains watching warily, as distant drums hint at unrest beyond the palace walls.

dialogue.text: When Kapilendra Gajapati died, he left an empire from the Ganga to the Kaveri—and a throne that did not wish to be shared. His son Purushottama sat upon it, but his brother Hamvira did not bow.

i18n.hi: कपिलेंद्र गजपति के जाते ही गंगा से कावेरी तक साम्राज्य तो मिला, पर सिंहासन किसी के साथ बाँटने को तैयार न था। पुत्र पुरुषोत्तम बैठा, पर भाई हाम्वीर ने सिर न झुकाया।

panels.shot: broad bird’s-eye over map-like landscape, showing arrows and rival hosts converging
panels.action: A sweeping view over stylized plains and rivers suggests the Eastern Ghats, with two great armies facing each other: one bearing the white elephant banners of the Gajapatis, the other marked by a rival royal standard.

dialogue.text: Civil war tore the Gajapati realm. Hamvira claimed his father’s mantle; Purushottama clung to Cuttack and Puri. Fort by fort, field by field, brothers turned the land of Jagannath into a battleground.

i18n.hi: गजपति राज्य गृहयुद्ध में फट गया। हाम्वीर ने पिता की गद्दी माँगी, पुरुषोत्तम कट्टक और पुरी से चिपका रहा। किला–किला, खेत–खेत, भाइयों ने जगन्नाथ की धरती को रणभूमि बना दिया।

panels.shot: medium shot at a balcony overlooking the Mahanadi, dusk light, reflective mood
panels.action: Purushottama Deva stands at a stone balcony above a broad river, armor loosened, eyes shadowed, as a small train of refugees and soldiers trudges along the far bank.

dialogue.text: Purushottama was no invincible conqueror at first. Hamvira won allies, seized strongholds, battered his brother’s claim. The Gajapati throne, for a time, seemed balanced on a river’s edge.

i18n.hi: शुरू में पुरुषोत्तम कोई अजेय विजेता न था। हाम्वीर ने साथी जोड़े, गढ़ छीने, भाई का दावा डगमगाया। कुछ समय को गजपति सिंहासन मानो नदी के किनारे डगमगा रहा था।

panels.shot: close-up on Purushottama’s face in temple light, hands folded in resolve
panels.action: Inside the sanctum glow of Jagannath’s temple at Puri, Purushottama Deva kneels with folded hands before the unseen deity, the faint outline of the wooden icons just hinted in darkness.

dialogue.text: In Puri, the new king turned to the temple that anchored his house. The Gajapatis were mahaprabhu’s servants before they were emperors. Purushottama staked his broken authority on that bond.

i18n.hi: पुरी में नए राजा ने उस मंदिर का सहारा लिया जिसने उसके कुल को थाम रखा था। गजपति पहले महाप्रभु के सेवक थे, फिर सम्राट। पुरुषोत्तम ने टूटी सत्ता उस बंधन पर दाँव पर लगाई।

panels.shot: ceremonial low-angle shot in front of the chariot, crowded courtyard, focus on broom in royal hand
panels.action: Under the blazing sun of Ratha Yatra, Purushottama Deva in full regalia bends slightly forward, both hands gripping a rich golden-handled broom as he sweeps the path before Jagannath’s towering wooden chariot, watched by courtiers and commoners alike.

dialogue.text: So the king took up the broom. In the chariot festival of Puri, he swept the road before Jagannath’s car, calling himself not lord but sweeper of the Lord of the World. The act stunned friend and rival alike.

i18n.hi: तभी राजा ने झाड़ू उठा ली। रथयात्रा में उसने जगन्नाथ के रथ से पहले मार्ग बुहारा, खुद को स्वामी नहीं, जग के स्वामी का झाड़ूदार कहा। यह दृश्य मित्र–शत्रु सबको सन्न कर गया।

panels.shot: medium shot with foreign envoys in foreground, their backs to viewer, watching the ritual
panels.action: Two richly dressed southern envoys stand in the shadow of the crowd, their faces a mix of surprise and disdain as they gaze at Purushottama sweeping, while the chariot looms behind.

dialogue.text: Later Odia chronicles would tell a sharp tale: that envoys from mighty Vijayanagara saw this royal sweeper, laughed, and refused a marriage alliance, saying a man who swept could not wed their princess.

i18n.hi: बाद के ओड़िया लेखों ने कड़ा किस्सा जोड़ा: विजयनगर के दूतों ने इस झाड़ू लगाते राजा को देखा, हँसे, और बोले—जो आदमी झाड़ू लगाए, वह हमारी राजकुमारी से ब्याह नहीं कर सकता।

panels.shot: cutaway to manuscript close-up, hands pointing at text, candlelight flicker
panels.action: A palm-leaf manuscript lies open under lamplight, a scholar’s hand tracing the engraved lines, while another hand, belonging to a modern historian, rests beside printed books.

dialogue.text: The Madala Panji preserves this Kanchi-Kaveri legend. Historians warn it is a late, layered memory, a story shaped by temple pride. Yet behind it stands a real collision between Odisha and Vijayanagara.

i18n.hi: मदला पंजी ने ही यह कांची–कावेरी कथा सँभाल रखी है। इतिहासकार कहते हैं, यह देर से बनी, परतदार याद है, मंदिर-गौरव से तराशी कहानी। पर इसके पीछे ओड़िशा और विजयनगर की असली टक्कर छिपी है।

panels.shot: wide shot of Kanchipuram and Southern forts, temple gopuram and hill-fort juxtaposed
panels.action: A panoramic view shows the tall gopuram of Kanchipuram rising above tiled roofs, with distant hill forts like Udayagiri silhouetted beyond, as banners of Vijayanagara snap in the dry wind.

dialogue.text: By the 1470s, Purushottama’s south lay under strain. Saluva Narasimha, the strongman of Vijayanagara, watched the Gajapati’s coastal holdings and inland forts at places like Udayagiri, waiting for weakness.

i18n.hi: १४७० के दशक तक पुरुषोत्तम का दक्षिण हिस्सा दबाव में था। विजयनगर का बलशाली सलुवा नरसिंह, गजपति के समुंदर किनारे के बंदरगाह और उदयगिरि जैसे पहाड़ी गढ़ों पर नज़र रखे कमजोरी की घड़ी तौल रहा था।

panels.shot: dynamic split-screen style composition, one side Gajapati army mustering, other side Vijayanagara forces arming
panels.action: On one side, Odia war elephants and archers gather under white elephant banners; on the other, armored Vijayanagara cavalry and infantry form up beneath a sun-emblazoned standard, both forces poised to march south and north respectively.

dialogue.text: First came setbacks. In the south, Odia positions bent under pressure. Forts changed hands. But neither side could simply walk away. The borderlands between Kanchi and the Kaveri became a chessboard of sieges and raids.

i18n.hi: पहले तो झटके ही लगे। दक्षिण में ओड़िया मोर्चे दबने लगे, किले हाथ बदलते गए। पर कोई भी पक्ष यूँ ही लौट नहीं सकता था। कांची–कावेरी की सरहद घेराबंदियों और धावों की बसात बन गई।

panels.shot: heroic medium-wide of Purushottama mounted, army behind, marching through rocky pass
panels.action: Clad in mail and crowned, Purushottama Deva rides at the head of his army through a rocky Eastern Ghats pass, elephants and infantry stretching behind him, dust rising as priests carry portable icons among the ranks.

dialogue.text: When his throne was secure, Purushottama struck south. He could not erase the insult woven into legend, but he could answer it with steel and resolve. The Gajapati banners moved again toward Kanchi country.

i18n.hi: गद्दी पक्की होते ही पुरुषोत्तम दक्षिण पर टूटा। कथा में बुने अपमान को वह मिटा तो नहीं सकता था, पर तलवार और जिद से उसका जवाब दे सकता था। गजपति के ध्वज फिर कांची देश की ओर बढ़ चले।

panels.shot: mid-range siege shot of Udayagiri-type hill fort under attack, without close violence
panels.action: An immense hill fort rises from rocky slopes, its walls bristling with defenders as Odia soldiers push siege ladders upward and war elephants batter at a gate, while Vijayanagara archers loose arrows from above.

dialogue.text: The struggle hardened around fortified hills like Udayagiri. These were not quick field clashes but grinding sieges, month after month, as each side tried to pry the other from the granite spines of the Deccan.

i18n.hi: संघर्ष उदयगिरि जैसे किलेदार पहाड़ों पर अटक गया। यह बिजली-सी भिड़ंत नहीं, महीनों की घिसटती घेराबंदियाँ थीं, जहाँ दोनों ताकतें दक्कन की ग्रेनाइट रीढ़ से एक-दूसरे को उखाड़ने में लगी थीं।

panels.shot: solemn interior shot of a shrine being dismantled, focus on artisans lowering a deity image
panels.action: Inside a stone temple, priests and soldiers carefully lower a bronze Ganapati icon from its niche, while scribes note its removal and guards stand watch, suggesting an organized, deliberate seizure.

dialogue.text: In this war of kings, gods too were taken captive. Odia memories speak of Uchchhishta Ganapati and other images seized from southern shrines, lifted from their sanctums as trophies of victory and tokens of divine favor.

i18n.hi: राजाओं की इस जंग में देवता भी क़ैद किए गए। ओड़िया यादें उच्छिष्ट गणपति और दूसरे दक्षिणी देवमूर्तियों का ज़िक्र करती हैं, जिन्हें मंदिरों से उठा कर विजय-निशान और देव-कृपा की जामिन बना लाया गया।

panels.shot: processional wide shot of Odia army returning north with carts bearing covered icons
panels.action: The Odia army winds along a coastal road at sunset, carts in the middle bearing shrouded divine images, guarded by soldiers, while behind them the silhouettes of distant southern temples fade into the orange haze.

dialogue.text: Eaton and Wagoner would later describe this as sacred politics: icons captured, not to be broken, but to proclaim that one king had humbled another, that one temple had, for a time, mastered its rival.

i18n.hi: ईटन और वागनर ने इसे बाद में ‘पवित्र राजनीति’ कहा—मूर्तियाँ तोड़ी नहीं गईं, बल्कि यह जताने को पकड़ी गईं कि एक राजा ने दूसरे को झुका दिया, एक मंदिर ने थोड़े समय को अपने प्रतिद्वंदी को मात दे दी।

panels.shot: regal interior wide shot of a Vijayanagara-style hall with envoys in negotiation
panels.action: In a pillared Vijayanagara hall, nobles in jeweled turbans and Odia representatives in distinct dress sit opposite each other, tension in their postures, as a rolled treaty document lies between them.

dialogue.text: The wars did not end in annihilation. They ended, as powerful rivalries often did, in treaty. Saluva Narasimha’s court and the Gajapati’s men bargained in stone halls, measuring forts, revenues, and pride.

i18n.hi: युद्ध विनाश पर नहीं, समझौते पर थमे। जैसा ताकतवर बैरियों में अक्सर होता है, सलुवा नरसिंह की दरबार और गजपति के दूत पत्थर के महलों में बैठे–बैठे किले, आय और मान घटा–बढ़ा कर सौदे करने लगे।

panels.shot: ceremonial wedding wide shot, Odia and southern motifs blended, bride in palanquin
panels.action: A richly veiled princess carried in a palanquin arrives at a decorated courtyard where Odia and southern architectural motifs intertwine, musicians playing as dignitaries from both realms look on.

dialogue.text: Out of those negotiations grew a marriage alliance. Odia tradition names her Padmavati, a Vijayanagara princess given to Purushottama. The wedding did what swords could not: it bound two courts in uneasy kinship.

i18n.hi: इन ही बातों–पातों से एक नया सगाई–संबंध निकला। ओड़िया परंपरा उसे पद्मावती कहती है, विजयनगर की राजकुमारी जो पुरुषोत्तम को दी गई। यह शादी वह कर गई जो तलवारें न कर सकीं—दो दरबारों को बेचैन रिश्तेदारी में बाँध दिया।

panels.shot: medium shot of Purushottama and his queen before an installed trophy icon in Puri
panels.action: In a side-shrine at Puri, Purushottama Deva stands beside his queen, both gazing up at a newly installed Ganapati image, priests chanting behind them as lamps glow on the deity’s polished surface.

dialogue.text: In Puri, the captured Ganapati found a new home under Jagannath’s gaze. To Purushottama’s court, it signaled that the sweeper of the Lord had answered insult with campaign and come back with both bride and deity.

i18n.hi: पुरी में पकड़ा गया गणपति, जगन्नाथ की निगरानी में नया आसन पा गया। पुरुषोत्तम की राजसभा के लिए यह संकेत था—प्रभु का झाड़ूदार अपमान का जवाब युद्ध से दे कर वधू और देव, दोनों को साथ लेकर लौटा।

panels.shot: parallel composition: left half Purushottama sweeping the chariot, right half him leading troops
panels.action: The frame splits: on one side, Purushottama in royal robes sweeps before Jagannath’s chariot in Puri; on the other, he strides in armor at the head of his army, elephants behind him, the same steady resolve in both faces.

dialogue.text: The legend remembers a king who was mocked for sweeping and then proved his might in war. The record shows a more complex truth: humility at Puri, hard campaigns in the south, treaties and trophies, loss and gain intertwined.

i18n.hi: कथा याद रखती है एक राजा को, जो झाड़ू पर हँसाया गया और फिर रण में अपनी ताकत दिखा गया। दस्तावेज़ बताते हैं ज्यादा उलझी सच्चाई—पुरी की विनम्रता, दक्षिण की कठिन मुहिमें, संधियाँ और जीत के साथ हारें गुँथी हुईं।

panels.shot: final contemplative wide shot atop Puri’s walls, sea and temple in view, twilight
panels.action: At twilight atop the walls near Puri, Purushottama Deva stands alone, the spire of Jagannath’s temple and the distant shimmer of the sea behind him, his broom and sword resting side by side at his feet.

dialogue.text: In Purushottama’s story, the broom and the blade stand together. His age reminds us that a king’s greatest power may lie not only in victory over enemies, but in the symbol he chooses to kneel before.

i18n.hi: पुरुषोत्तम की कहानी में झाड़ू और तलवार साथ खड़ी हैं। उसका युग याद दिलाता है कि राजा की सबसे बड़ी ताकत केवल दुश्मन हराने में नहीं, उस निशान में भी हो सकती है जिसके आगे वह घुटने टेकने को चुनता है।

subtitle_i18n.en: From Civil War to Kanchi-Kaveri: The Humbling of a Gajapati
subtitle_i18n.hi: गृहयुद्ध से कांची–कावेरी तक: झुका एक गजपति
